text: Over the last 30 days, some visitors raised concerns about overcrowding, especially during school group visits, which limited access to exhibits. Several critical reviews focused on the heavy use of AI in the exhibits, describing it as distracting or lacking educational depth, with some visitors feeling it did not honor Roosevelt’s legacy. A few noted the absence of an introductory film and desired more detailed historical content. Positive comments often mentioned the interactive exhibits and the building’s architecture, but the balance between technology and substantive interpretation remains an area needing attention.

windows.7: Over the past week, visitor reviews for the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library have been uniformly positive, with no critical feedback reported. Several comments highlighted the interactive exhibits as a key aspect of the experience, while others noted the quality of interpretation and the building’s architecture. Staff and food and beverage services were also mentioned positively in a few reviews. There were isolated remarks about dwell time, timed entry, and considerations for different age groups, but these were less frequent.
